title: POST /api/v1/indicator-statistics — one element of the request array (v6 pipeline, XAUUSD)
description: Contract between the push worker (backfill_worker_api_gateway_v5.py) and the API Gateway for the APPEND-ONLY indicator statistics stream. One JSON object = one indicator's _Statistic.txt snapshot for one collection cycle. The request body is an ARRAY of these (one cycle produces up to 12, and they are pushed together). This stream is entirely separate from market_data: it has its own endpoint, queue and outbox, and a failure here must never block the market_data path. The gateway MUST upsert idempotently on (symbol, timeframe, source, captured_at) — duplicate delivery is by design (push retries) — but the content of a re-push is byte-identical, so rows are never meaningfully mutated. Correcting a value means a NEW row with a later captured_at, never an update.

terminal_id.description: Sender id; 'push_worker_v5' from the v6 push worker.

source.description: Which indicator produced this snapshot. The 3 non-centroid line sources omit the MODEL A block; resistance/support additionally omit the EDT channel (single lines, not channels). sr_levels and sr2_levels (the 14th and 15th indicators, the same Freedman-Diaconis engine run as two independently anchored instances) are calibration documents rather than regression fits: they populate the sr_* fields and leave the model/channel fields null. This enum is CLOSED and the request is an ARRAY, so a sender using a value the deployed gateway does not know will 400 the WHOLE batch -- deploy the gateway before the VPS starts sending a new source.

captured_at.description: WHEN the fit was observed — the collector's 5-minute cycle slot (UTC unix sec). This is the half of the primary key that makes the table append-only: it is new on every cycle, so a new row never collides with an old one.

live_bar_ts.description: Newest bar present in that source's timeseries export at capture time; joins to market_data_v6.timestamp. Ties the fit to the exact bar it was anchored at.

cycle_id.description: provenance: the collection_cycles row this snapshot came from.

properties._resolved_line_note: All 10 sources: the line the indicator settled on. solution_found/line_origin_ts/touches are only emitted by the 3 line indicators; the centroids leave them null.

window_bars.description: centroids: Observation Window (Box B Bars). Bar Coverage is derived from this.

properties._model_a_note: [MODEL A; CROSSINGS] — residuals against the SSA crossing points. CENTROIDS ONLY; the line indicators have no crossings and leave these null.
properties._model_b_note: [MODEL B; CLOSE PRICE] — residuals against close prices. All 10 sources. NOTE these lines are fitted to centroids or fractal touches, NOT to closes, so a low or negative R2 is structurally expected and is not by itself a fault; containment_rate is the more direct quality measure.
properties._edt_note: [EDT CHANNEL] — the 7 centroids + fractal_edt only. Offsets are baseline-relative. resistance/support are single lines and leave these null.

containment_rate.description: Percent of the fitted window that closed inside the channel.

_extended_note.description: Marker only. Extended statistics [added 2026-09-20]: [FIT WINDOW], [PRICE CONTEXT], [CHANNEL GEOMETRY] and the two [RESIDUAL DIAGNOSTICS] blocks, written with identical labels by every indicator. All optional and nullable: a field is null when it does not apply to that source, or when the terminal still runs a binary that predates the block. Never zero-filled -- 0.0 is a real reading for most of them.

window_span_bars.description: bars from the leftmost evaluated bar to the live bar, inclusive

visual_window_bars.description: bars the channel is DRAWN over (can exceed the evaluated window)

bars_available.description: bars the indicator actually had; distinguishes a short fit from a short chart

leftmost_bar_index.description: index of the oldest evaluated bar, for reproducing the fit

line_span_bars.description: bars between the oldest and newest resolved baseline value

baseline_coverage_n.description: bars in that span carrying a resolved baseline

baseline_coverage_rate.description: percent; 100 * baseline_coverage_n / line_span_bars, gaps show up as < 100

centroids_used.description: centroids the winning fit actually used; null for non-centroid sources

crossings_in_window_n.description: SSA crossings inside the drawn span (crossings_n counts the evaluated window)

first_crossing_ts.description: unix UTC of the oldest crossing in that span

last_crossing_ts.description: unix UTC of the newest; with first_crossing_ts this dates the evidence the fit rests on

live_close.description: close of the newest bar, so the snapshot is self-contained

baseline_value.description: fitted baseline AT the live bar (not the y-intercept)

uoedt_value.description: upper band price at the live bar

loedt_value.description: lower band price at the live bar

dist_to_uoedt.description: uoedt_value - live_close; negative means price is above the band

dist_to_loedt.description: live_close - loedt_value; negative means price is below the band

channel_position.description: 0 at LOEDT, 1 at UOEDT; outside [0,1] means price has left the channel

window_high.description: highest high across the resolved span

window_low.description: lowest low across the resolved span

window_range.description: window_high - window_low; the scale channel_width should be read against

channel_asymmetry.description: (uoedt_offset + loedt_offset) / width; 0 = symmetric. Reported, never penalised: EDT bands come from outermost touches, so asymmetry is often a true reading

breach_above_n.description: closes above the upper band; containment_rate alone cannot say which side price left from

max_excursion_above.description: worst close-above-band distance; null when there was none

max_excursion_below.description: worst close-below-band distance; null when there was none

resid_a_n.description: sample for the crossings residual diagnostics; measured over the DRAWN span, which need not equal model_a_n

resid_a_mean.description: bias: a line parallel to price but offset from it still scores well on MSE

resid_a_sd.description: dispersion around that bias, in price units

resid_a_dw.description: serial correlation; ~2 independent, <1 means a straight line is the wrong MODEL here, not merely a badly fitted one

resid_b_n.description: sample for the close-price residual diagnostics

resid_b_dw.description: the diagnostic model_b_r2 cannot give: these lines are fitted to centroids or touches and then scored against closes, so r2 is routinely negative

_sr_note.description: Marker only. [SUPPORT-RESISTANCE AUTO-CALIBRATION] provenance [added 2026-09-20], populated by sr_levels and sr2_levels only and null for every other source. sr_1..sr_16 are not carried here: they already reach Postgres through market_data. These record WHY those levels exist.

sr_fractals_n.description: fractals the Freedman-Diaconis calibration was computed from; a small N means a wide, unreliable step

sr_iqr.description: interquartile range; the dispersion the bucket width is derived from

sr_optimal_step.description: auto-calibrated bucket width. THE field: every sr_* level in market_data (sr_1..sr_8 for sr_levels, sr_9..sr_16 for sr2_levels) is a bucket of this size, and nothing downstream could previously tell how wide they were

sr_macro_clusters.description: clusters found before the 8-slot pipeline truncation; > 8 means levels were dropped

sr_nearest_resistance.description: closest level above the live close

sr_dist_resistance_pts.description: distance to it in POINTS, not price -- the indicator's own unit, kept as exported

config_hash.description: sha256 of the normalised parameter block. Deduplicates configuration out of this fact table — the params are compiled into the .mq5 and change only on redeploy, so storing them inline would repeat an identical blob on every row. A NEW hash appearing is itself the drift signal (the indicator was reconfigured).

config_params.description: The parameter block verbatim, as parsed key/value pairs. The gateway creates the indicator_configs row on first sight of a hash and ignores it thereafter.

x-gateway-requirements.batching: The request body is an ARRAY of these objects (up to 10 per cycle). The gateway enqueues one job PER ELEMENT so per-row idempotency is preserved across a batched request.
x-gateway-requirements.idempotency: Upsert on (symbol, timeframe, source, captured_at). Duplicate delivery is by design (push retries); re-pushed content is byte-identical, so this never mutates history.
x-gateway-requirements.append_only: Rows are NEVER updated with different content and NEVER deleted. A correction is a new row with a later captured_at.
x-gateway-requirements.isolation: This endpoint is independent of POST /api/v1/market-data. Its failure must not affect market_data ingestion in any way.

responses.400: Validation failure with JSON {message}. Worker quarantines to rejected_statistics.jsonl AND stamps synced_at (poison-row guard).
responses.401/403: Auth failure — worker halts this stream only.
